issues.change: Replaced the option 'by' with 'to' and restored targetFeature to preposition_of_clock_time. Options are now on / in / at / to, key 'at' unchanged at index 2.
issues.whyThisOptionAndNotStemContext: The register's option (a) - which Step 2C wrongly rejected - is the right fix. Adding stem context to license 'by' would have kept a second licit preposition in play and made the construct depend on the learner noticing a clause. Removing 'by' makes every distractor wrong on the same grounds. 'to' was chosen because it is a genuine time-telling preposition ('ten to nine'), so it is a plausible learner error, and because 'starts to half past nine' has no licit reading at all. 'before' and 'around' were rejected for exactly the reason 'by' was: both remain semantically defensible.

The key was 58 characters against 28-48, so the longest-option heuristic pointed straight at it; it is now 38 and not the longest. My first rewrite used 'To ask for one more step before Friday' - and LST_Q_008's stem says 'the Friday deadline', so Q008's stem pointed at Q007's key. issues.change: All four options are now propositions about the deadline: Meeting it would avoid a month's delay / It applies only to new applications / It can be extended on request / It was set by the landlord, not the office. Key at index 0 unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: all four options are propositions about the deadline

REV-006: a reviewer given only stem and options cannot eliminate more than one option a priori
issues.validationResult: PASS, and the REV-006 criterion was executed rather than proxied. Running the elimination test on stem and options only: option 1 is plausible because deadlines commonly gate a processing cycle; option 2 is plausible because deadlines commonly scope to a category of application; option 3 is plausible because extensions are commonly available; option 4 is plausible because a third party could have set the date. A-priori eliminable count = 0, against a permitted maximum of 1. The previous set failed this test with 2 eliminable: 'It has already passed' was defeated by the stem's own framing of Friday as the deadline, and 'The landlord must send the page directly' was not about the deadline at all.
